description: Help on every card and control, the MoonWalk step a card takes part in, and the test that checks a control.

steps.title: Help and MoonWalk
steps.description: What each card does, and the steps around it
steps.caption: Help and MoonWalk. What each card does, and the steps around it.
Help is off by default, so the cards stay compact. The i button in the top bar turns it on.
The first time, it asks before downloading: the help comes from the documentation site, not from the device. Once you agree, this browser remembers.
Every card now says what it is, in one line and a short summary.
And every control says what it does, right under it.
The arrow opens the rest of a card's help: its guide, and links to its catalog page, its source, its tests, and the MoonWalk steps it takes part in.
Help also links the processes a card takes part in. This one opens MoonWalk at the step that sizes the grid.
MoonWalk shows the whole process: its goal, each step, and which steps this device has already done.
Where a step has a clip, it plays right here, beside the step it shows.
Close it, and you are back where you were.
A control's help also names the tests that check it.
Here is brightness, on the Drivers card, with the scenarios that set it.
This one opens the test page at the scenario that sets brightness and checks what the lights do. Every behavior has a test like it.
The map button opens all of MoonWalk: every process, what this device has done, and what comes next.
Pick any process to see its steps.
Close the map, and the cards are where you left them.
The same i button turns help off again. Help and MoonWalk: what each card does, how to do things with it, and what proves it works.
